# ObsidianUltra

> A fork of the Obsidian UI library (deividcomsono/Obsidian) for Roblox exploit scripts.
> Everything from upstream Obsidian works unchanged; this file documents only what this
> fork adds, because an LLM that knows upstream Obsidian will not know about these.

Load it the same way as upstream, but from this repo:

```lua
local repo = "https://raw.githubusercontent.com/joustingmatch/ObsidianUltra/main/"
local Library = loadstring(game:HttpGet(repo .. "Library.lua"))()
```

Types for both features live in `Library.d.luau`; `Example.lua` has runnable usage.

## Sub tabs (tabs inside a tab)

A sub tab is a second level of tabs *inside* one sidebar tab. They render as a row of
buttons across the top of the tab's content area, above the groupboxes. This is not the
same thing as a **Tabbox** — a Tabbox is a small tabbed widget that lives inside one
column, while a sub tab owns the entire content area and has its own left and right
columns.

### Creating them

```lua
local Combat = Window:AddTab("Combat", "swords")

local PvP = Combat:AddSubTab("PvP")                                 -- name, icon
local Parry = Combat:AddSubTab("Parry", "shield")
local Builder = Combat:AddSubTab({ Name = "Builder", Icon = "wrench" })  -- table form
```

`Tab:AddSubTab` accepts either `(Name: string, Icon: string?)` or a
`{ Name: string, Icon: string? }` table, mirroring `Window:AddTab`. The icon is optional
and resolves through the same lucide lookup as everywhere else.

### What a sub tab supports

A sub tab is tab-like: it has its own `Sides` (left and right `ScrollingFrame`s), so every
container method a tab has works on it, and the elements inside behave identically.

```lua
PvP:AddLeftGroupbox("Aiming", "crosshair"):AddToggle("SilentAim", { Text = "Silent Aim" })
PvP:AddRightGroupbox("Targeting"):AddDropdown("HitPart", { Values = { "Head" }, Default = 1 })

local Box = Builder:AddLeftTabbox("Animation Builder")   -- tabboxes nest inside sub tabs
Box:AddTab("Timings"):AddToggle("Preview", { Text = "Preview" })
```

Available on a sub tab: `AddGroupbox`, `AddLeftGroupbox`, `AddRightGroupbox`, `AddTabbox`,
`AddLeftTabbox`, `AddRightTabbox`, `Show`, `Hide`, `SetVisible`, `Hover`, `Resize`,
`RefreshSides`, `Destroy`.

Fields: `Type` (`"SubTab"`), `Name`, `Window`, `Tab` (the parent tab), `Canvas`, `Button`,
`Sides`, `Groupboxes`, `Tabboxes`, `DependencyGroupboxes`.

### Alignment

The button row is centered by default:

```lua
Combat:SetSubTabAlignment("Left")   -- "Left" | "Center" | "Right"
```

The active sub tab is drawn as a rounded chip: a fill lighter than `MainColor`, a thin
outline, an accent label, and a bar under it that gradients from the font colour at both
ends to the accent colour in the middle (fading out at the edges). Idle sub tabs are label
only at 40% transparency; hover sits between the two.

### Behaviour worth knowing

- **The parent tab becomes a host.** The moment a tab gets its first sub tab, that tab's
  own left/right columns are hidden. Put your groupboxes on the sub tabs, not on the
  parent tab — anything already added to the parent will disappear from view.
- The first sub tab added is shown automatically. `SubTab:Show()` switches to one;
  switching reuses the window's tab transition animation settings.
- `SubTab:SetVisible(false)` hides its button and, if it was active, falls through to
  another visible sub tab.
- Search works across sub tabs. Sub tabs whose elements do not match the query have their
  buttons hidden, and if the active sub tab has no matches the search jumps to one that
  does.
- Warning boxes still belong to the parent tab (`Tab:UpdateWarningBox`), and the sub tab
  content is offset below both the warning box and the button row.

### Related tab members

- `Tab.SubTabs` — `{ [Name]: SubTab }`
- `Tab.ActiveSubTab` — the visible sub tab, or `nil`
- `Tab:GetContentOffset()` — pixels reserved at the top of the tab by the warning box and
  the sub tab row
- `Library:GetActiveSides()` — the `ScrollingFrame`s currently on screen; returns the
  active sub tab's sides when there is one, otherwise the active tab's. Prefer this over
  `Library.ActiveTab.Sides`, which is wrong whenever sub tabs are in use.

## Header

The header was reworked and differs from upstream in ways that affect script authors:

- **The open tab is always named in the header.** Upstream only showed the header tab info
  when a tab was given a `Description`; here the bold tab name is always shown, with the
  description as a smaller faded second line when there is one. Give tabs a `Description`
  to fill that second line:
  `Window:AddTab({ Name = "Main", Icon = "user", Description = "Main features" })`
- `Window:ShowTabInfo(Name, Description)` accepts a `nil`/empty description and hides the
  second line instead of leaving a blank one.
- **The search box is a pill** (fully rounded, icon inset on the left, placeholder
  `"Search..."`). It is registered in `Library.PillCorners`, a third corner list added by
  this fork: those corners stay fully rounded at any corner radius above 0, and go square
  when the radius is set to 0, so the pill still obeys `Window:SetCornerRadius(0)`.
- `SearchbarSize` now defaults to `UDim2.fromScale(0.35, 1)` rather than
  `UDim2.fromScale(1, 1)`, and the box no longer resizes itself when tab info appears —
  the tab info grows to fill whatever the search box does not use. Pass your own
  `SearchbarSize` to override.

## Copyable footer

The footer is a row of segments, and each segment is either plain text or a copy target.
A copyable segment is drawn in `Library.Scheme.BlueColor` at full opacity so it reads as a
link, and gets its own small copy button; clicking the text or the button writes that
segment to the clipboard and flips the icon to a check for about 1.5 seconds. Plain
segments keep the usual 50% faded white.

### A single string

`Footer` accepts a plain string, and `CopyableFooter` (default `true`) decides whether the
whole thing is copyable:

```lua
Library:CreateWindow({
    Footer = "version: example",
    CopyableFooter = true,   -- false gives the plain grey footer
})
```

### Mixed plain and copyable text

Pass a list instead. **Bare strings are plain text**, and a table segment is only copyable
when it says `Copyable = true` — copyability is opt in per segment, and `CopyableFooter`
does not apply to this form:

```lua
Library:CreateWindow({
    Footer = {
        "version: example |",                                   -- plain
        { Text = "discord.gg/mspaint", Copyable = true },        -- blue + copy button
        "|",
        { Text = "user id", Copyable = true, CopyText = "123" }, -- copies CopyText
    },
})
```

Segment fields: `Text` (shown), `Copyable` (defaults to `false` in list form), `CopyText`
(what lands on the clipboard, defaults to `Text` — use it when the label should not be the
copied value).

Segments are laid out in a centered horizontal row with 6px between them, so put any
separators (`"|"`, `"-"`) in as their own plain segments.

### Runtime and caveats

- `Window:SetFooter(Footer)` takes either form and rebuilds the row, replacing whatever was
  there. It used to accept only a string.
- The clipboard writer is resolved once at load as
  `setclipboard or toclipboard or syn.write_clipboard`. If the executor exposes none of
  them, every segment falls back to plain text and no copy buttons are created — do not
  assume they exist.

### Scheme.BlueColor

This fork adds one scheme colour, used for the footer highlight and available to your own
elements:

- `Library.Scheme.BlueColor`, default `Color3.fromRGB(80, 155, 255)`
- Alias `"Blue"` — any property that accepts a scheme string accepts `"Blue"` or
  `"BlueColor"`, and it re-colours automatically when the theme changes
- `ThemeManager` preserves it across theme swaps, like `RedColor` and `DarkColor`
